bank-of-england-fsr-ai-equity-concentrat.rationale: The existing s8_ai_capex story tracks capex-vs-revenue gaps and GPU-backed debt stress, but has no indicator for the systemic risk that AI equity concentration poses to broader financial stability—the channel the BoE FSR formally identifies. A narrow set of AI companies now drive a disproportionate share of global index returns; a revaluation event would cascade into sovereign debt markets (via fiscal multiplier expectations) and leveraged positions. This gap indicator captures that tail risk and would currently sit at '1 elevated'.

boj-holds-at-1-today-jul-31-with-hawkish.headline: BOJ holds at 1% today (Jul 31) with hawkish tilt; yen near 40-year low, 10-yr JGB hit 30-yr high of 2.90%
boj-holds-at-1-today-jul-31-with-hawkish.summary: The Bank of Japan kept its policy rate at 1% in an 8-1 vote on July 31, with one dissenter calling for an immediate hike to 1.25%; Governor Ueda's press conference was read as moderately hawkish, signalling October/December tightening. The yen traded near 164/USD—a four-decade low—forcing suspected MoF intervention overnight, while the 10-yr JGB spiked to 2.90% (30-year high) earlier this month amid fiscal-expansion concerns and ~$29.6 bn of US Treasury selling by Japanese investors in Q1 2026.
boj-holds-at-1-today-jul-31-with-hawkish.target_indicator: USD/JPY (yen strengthening = lower = risk) + 30-year JGB yield (%)
boj-holds-at-1-today-jul-31-with-hawkish.rationale: Three s2_japan indicators are simultaneously flashing: USD/JPY at ~163-164 (historic weakness), 10-yr JGB at 2.90% (30-yr high, with 20-yr at 3.90%), and fiscal-plan clarity = 2 (disorderly—Takaichi blueprint language on BOJ alignment spooked markets). Japanese capital repatriation ($29.6 bn UST sold in Q1) also feeds directly into s1_basis_trade and s21_clearinghouses Treasury volatility. This is the highest-materiality single item in the tracker this week.

iea-warns-china-rare-earth-curbs-put-6-5.headline: IEA warns China rare-earth curbs put $6.5 tn in downstream production at risk; Nov-2026 suspension expiry looms
iea-warns-china-rare-earth-curbs-put-6-5.summary: A July 16 IEA report quantified that full enforcement of China's expanded rare-earth export controls could imperil $6.5 trillion in downstream production outside China. China widened entity-level controls to 10 US firms (June) and 14 EU firms (July 2026); the November 2025 one-year suspension of broader gallium/germanium/antimony controls expires in ~4 months, and H1 2026 export volumes are already 6.4% below H1 2025.
iea-warns-china-rare-earth-curbs-put-6-5.target_indicator: Nov-2025 pause status (0 extended / 1 expiring / 2 lapsed) + US domestic RE producer blacklist (0 none / 1 entity-specific ban / 2 sector-wide ban)
iea-warns-china-rare-earth-curbs-put-6-5.rationale: Nov-pause status should move toward 1 (expiring): the suspension runs to November 2026 and the IEA is pre-warning markets on full-enforcement risk. Entity blacklist indicator should move to 1 (entity-specific): 10 US and 14 EU firms now named. The $6.5 tn IEA figure is a new, material data point that raises the urgency of tracking the countdown to November. Also affects s8_ai_capex (GPU supply chains) and s19_lithography (chip inputs).

japan-fiscal-dominance-risk-takaichi-bas.headline: Japan fiscal-dominance risk: Takaichi 'Basic Policy' blueprint pressured BOJ independence; JGB fiscal premium widening
japan-fiscal-dominance-risk-takaichi-bas.summary: Japan's economic blueprint ('Basic Policy') included language calling on the BOJ to align monetary policy with growth objectives, triggering a 'Basic Policy shock' spike in JGB yields; a cabinet minister subsequently reaffirmed BOJ autonomy, but the episode revealed political pressure on rate-setting independence. Japanese investors sold $29.6 bn of US Treasuries in Q1 2026, and the 20-yr JGB touched 3.90%—a direct transmission channel to global long-end rates.

proposed_indicator.label: BOJ_independence_pressure
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = no government pressure on BOJ rate-setting; 1 = verbal pressure / policy-document language aligning BOJ with fiscal goals; 2 = sustained interference or de-facto fiscal dominance (BOJ forced to buy bonds to cap yields)

japan-fiscal-dominance-risk-takaichi-bas.rationale: The existing s2_japan indicators (USD/JPY, 30-yr JGB yield, Takaichi-plan financing clarity) do not capture the distinct risk of fiscal-dominance pressure on BOJ independence—separate from the spending plan itself. The 'Basic Policy shock' episode shows this is an actionable, discrete trigger: if language forcing BOJ accommodation returns, it changes the rate-path probability distribution and the JGB carry-trade unwind timeline. Suggested weight 0.20 reflects it as a leading/qualitative indicator versus the market-price indicators already tracked.

global-disinflation-stalled-imf-revises-.headline: Global disinflation stalled; IMF revises 2026 headline inflation to 4.7% as Middle East war drives energy-price resurgence
global-disinflation-stalled-imf-revises-.summary: The IMF's July 8 WEO Update raised its 2026 global headline inflation forecast to 4.7%, stating that 'the disinflation trend in place since early 2024 has stalled' due to Middle East war-driven energy prices. The World Bank projects global growth slowing to 2.5%, with EMDEs facing their weakest per-capita income growth since the pandemic; the energy-import shock is hitting oil-importing developing economies hardest.

proposed_story.name: War-driven stagflation overhang
proposed_story.why: The US-Iran war and Hormuz disruption have re-ignited a global energy-price shock that has stalled disinflation and forced central banks outside the US into unexpected tightening. This creates a distinct macro risk channel—higher-for-longer rates in Europe, EM, and Japan simultaneously—that none of the existing stories fully captures. It is the binding macro constraint that amplifies s4_dev_debt, s2_japan, s10_france, and s18_food_fertilizer but operates at the global monetary-policy coordination level.

indicators.label: IMF_global_headline_inflation_forecast_pct
indicators.rubric: IMF WEO Update 2026 global headline CPI forecast (%). Baseline ~3.5%; elevated ≥4.0%; critical ≥4.5%

indicators.label: DM_ex_US_policy_rate_hike_surprise
indicators.rubric: 0 = ECB/BoE/RBA easing or on-hold as expected; 1 = unexpected hold or hawkish pivot in ≥1 major DM CB; 2 = coordinated DM tightening cycle resumed due to energy shock

indicators.label: Brent_crude_USD_bbl
indicators.rubric: Brent spot price. Below $75 = easing; $75-$95 = elevated; above $95 = critical/stagflationary

indicators.label: US_Iran_ceasefire_durability
indicators.rubric: 0 = durable ceasefire / Hormuz fully open; 1 = fragile MoU / contested passage; 2 = active hostilities / strait blockaded

global-disinflation-stalled-imf-revises-.rationale: No existing story in the tracker treats the war-stalled-disinflation channel as a primary risk. The IMF's upward revision to 4.7% global inflation and simultaneous growth downgrade is the canonical stagflation signal. Unlike s20_sea_lanes (physical chokepoint) or s4_dev_debt (EM balance-sheet), this story is about the monetary-policy response function of DM central banks being hijacked by an exogenous energy shock—forcing a tightening bias into an already fragile global credit cycle, with second-order effects on every leveraged balance sheet in the tracker.

fomc-july-29-three-hawks-dissent-for-rat.headline: FOMC July 29: Three hawks dissent for rate hike — most divided since 2016
fomc-july-29-three-hawks-dissent-for-rat.summary: The Fed voted 9-3 to hold rates at 3.5–3.75% on July 29, with Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan all dissenting in favor of a 25bp hike, citing inflation elevated above 2% for over five years and successive supply shocks. Markets now price a materially higher probability of a September hike, with the CME hike odds rising from ~11% to ~36% between July 15 and July 29.

proposed_story.name: US Re-tightening Shock / Sticky-Inflation Trap
proposed_story.why: After five-plus years of above-target inflation, a hawkish minority is now openly pushing for rate hikes while the majority holds. A September hike — or a market pre-pricing of one — would tighten financial conditions sharply, stress leveraged positions in Treasuries (s1), unwind carry trades (s2), reprice private credit (s3), and amplify EM capital outflows (s4). No existing story captures the FOMC fracture itself as the risk node.

indicators.label: FOMC dissent count (current meeting)
indicators.rubric: 0 = unanimous or 1 dissent; 1 = 2 dissents; 2 = 3+ dissents (present level = 2)

indicators.label: CME FedWatch September hike probability (%)
indicators.rubric: Track daily; >40% = elevated; >60% = acute re-pricing risk

indicators.label: US 2-year Treasury yield (%)
indicators.rubric: Proxy for near-term rate expectations; sustained move above 4.5% signals re-tightening being priced

indicators.label: FOMC inflation language shift (0 patient / 1 data-dependent tightening bias / 2 explicit hike signal)
indicators.rubric: Monitor post-meeting statements and minutes for easing-bias removal and hawkish re-framing

fomc-july-29-three-hawks-dissent-for-rat.rationale: A 9-3 FOMC split — the most hawkish division since September 2016 — is a new systemic node: it re-opens the rate-hike path, tightens financial conditions across all existing risk stories (Treasury basis, Japan carry, private credit, EM debt), and signals that the Fed's reaction function is genuinely uncertain. This is not captured in any existing story or indicator.

japan-yen-hits-40-year-low-10y-jgb-at-30.headline: Japan: Yen hits 40-year low, 10y JGB at 30-year high ~2.9%; BOJ holds but FX intervention suspected
japan-yen-hits-40-year-low-10y-jgb-at-30.summary: Japanese financial assets came under severe pressure in late July 2026, with USD/JPY reaching a 40-year low and the 10-year JGB yield touching 2.901% — its highest since 1996 — before Tokyo's suspected FX intervention triggered a sharp yen rally. The BOJ held rates at 1% on July 31 but acknowledged upside inflation risks from the Middle East conflict.
japan-yen-hits-40-year-low-10y-jgb-at-30.target_indicator: USD/JPY (yen strengthening = lower = risk); 30-year JGB yield (%)
japan-yen-hits-40-year-low-10y-jgb-at-30.rationale: USD/JPY at a 40-year low and 10y JGB at a 30-year high are direct, material updates to s2_japan's two core indicators. The BOJ hold with suspected FX intervention adds to Takaichi plan financing uncertainty (third indicator). The combination of a weaker yen, surging yields, and a BOJ trapped between inflation and fiscal fragility is exactly the scenario this story tracks.

japanese-investors-sold-29-6bn-of-us-tre.headline: Japanese investors sold $29.6bn of US Treasuries in Q1 2026 amid domestic yield surge — structural buyer withdrawal
japanese-investors-sold-29-6bn-of-us-tre.summary: As domestic JGB yields hit multi-decade highs, Japanese investors repatriated capital and sold $29.6 billion of US debt in Q1 2026 alone, removing one of the largest and most reliable foreign buyers from the US Treasury market at a time of large US fiscal deficits. This structural shift in demand directly pressures Treasury market function and the basis trade.

proposed_indicator.label: Japanese net purchases of US Treasuries (rolling 4-quarter, $bn, TIC data)
proposed_indicator.rubric: Positive = net buyer (supportive); 0 to -$30bn = declining support (caution); below -$30bn per quarter = structural withdrawal (stress). Current trajectory: approx. -$29.6bn in Q1 2026 alone.

japanese-investors-sold-29-6bn-of-us-tre.rationale: The existing s1_basis_trade story tracks SOFR-EFFR spreads, MOVE index, and SEC clearing progress, but has no indicator for the structural foreign-demand side of the Treasury market. Japan is the largest foreign holder of US Treasuries; net selling at this scale reduces the marginal bid that normally absorbs new issuance, amplifies the price impact of basis-trade unwinds, and interacts adversely with rising US fiscal deficits. This gap is material and operationalizable via monthly TIC data.

strait-of-hormuz-traffic-stall-brent-reb.headline: Strait of Hormuz traffic stall: Brent rebounds ~20% from early-July low as US-Iran deal frays
strait-of-hormuz-traffic-stall-brent-reb.summary: After a brief post-agreement lull, traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has stalled and Brent crude has rebounded close to 20% from its early-July post-US-Iran deal low, with the 30-day full restoration deadline passing without compliance. The IMF revised global headline inflation up to 4.7% for 2026, partly on energy costs, while the World Bank cut global growth to 2.5%.
strait-of-hormuz-traffic-stall-brent-reb.target_indicator: Hormuz/Red Sea status (0 open / 1 contested / 2 closed); WTI crude oil (USD/bbl)
strait-of-hormuz-traffic-stall-brent-reb.rationale: The Hormuz traffic stall and ~20% Brent rebound from deal lows is a direct, material update to s20_sea_lanes's primary indicators. The IMF's upward revision to 2026 global inflation to 4.7% — partly attributed to energy — and the World Bank's 2.5% global growth forecast confirm second-order macro transmission. The status should be moved from 0 (open) toward 1 (contested) given the stall in restoration.

imf-weo-july-2026-global-disinflation-st.headline: IMF WEO July 2026: Global disinflation 'stalled'; AI capex 'sowing seeds of macrofinancial instability'; headline inflation revised to 4.7%
imf-weo-july-2026-global-disinflation-st.summary: The IMF's July 2026 World Economic Outlook Update explicitly warned that global disinflation has stalled, revised 2026 global headline inflation up to 4.7%, and flagged that 'AI hype and exuberant financial markets could sow the seeds of macrofinancial instability' — a direct risk flag for s8_ai_capex's circular financing concern. Growth was held at 3.0% for 2026 but risks remain tilted to the downside.

proposed_indicator.label: IMF / BIS systemic AI-capex warning flag (0 none / 1 watch / 2 explicit risk scenario)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = no multilateral mention; 1 = IMF/BIS flags concern in flagship publication (current level = 1, per July 2026 WEO); 2 = IMF/BIS publishes dedicated stress scenario or FSB includes in systemic risk list

imf-weo-july-2026-global-disinflation-st.rationale: The IMF's explicit WEO language about AI-driven 'macrofinancial instability' seeds represents a meaningful escalation in multilateral risk recognition for s8_ai_capex. The existing indicators for s8 (US IG OAS, capex-revenue gap, GPU-backed debt stress) are market/corporate measures; there is no indicator tracking whether global financial supervisors and multilaterals have formally elevated this to a systemic concern, which is a leading signal that regulatory or market stress action may follow.

us-iran-war-triggers-structural-nickel-s.headline: US-Iran War Triggers Structural Nickel Supply-Chain Rupture via Sulfur/Hormuz Dependency
us-iran-war-triggers-structural-nickel-s.summary: S&P Global research (March 2026) found that while copper's direct exposure to the Hormuz closure is limited, the nickel market faces structural stress: high-pressure acid leach (HPAL) battery-grade nickel operations are critically dependent on sulfuric acid derived from sulfur shipments transiting the Strait, putting EV battery supply chains at risk of a processing-input squeeze that is not captured by any existing tracker story.

proposed_indicator.label: Battery-critical mineral processing input disruption (nickel/sulfur via Hormuz)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = sulfur/acid supply flowing normally to HPAL operations; 1 = Hormuz disruption causing elevated acid costs or spot shortages for battery-grade nickel producers; 2 = sustained HPAL curtailments or plant shutdowns due to input unavailability

us-iran-war-triggers-structural-nickel-s.rationale: The s20_sea_lanes story focuses on crude oil, WTI, and broad maritime disruption, but does not capture second-order supply-chain effects on critical battery inputs. HPAL nickel processing—essential for EV and grid-storage batteries—depends on sulfur shipments that transit Hormuz, creating a distinct vector that bridges s20 (sea lanes) and s16 (copper/electrification) without being captured by either. Adding this indicator to s20 would alert the tracker to EV supply-chain contagion from the ongoing Hormuz crisis.

us-iran-conflict-triggers-new-energy-cos.headline: US-Iran Conflict Triggers New Energy-Cost Shock on AI Data-Center Capex and Power Markets
us-iran-conflict-triggers-new-energy-cos.summary: The Hormuz crisis drove energy price spikes through Q1–Q2 2026, materially raising the operating cost base for AI data centers that are heavy electricity consumers; elevated oil and LNG prices feed into power-generation costs globally, adding a new upward pressure on hyperscaler economics at a moment when the AI capex-versus-revenue gap is already wide and GPU-backed debt financing is under stress.

proposed_indicator.label: Energy-cost drag on AI data-center economics (oil/LNG shock pass-through)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = energy costs stable or falling, no material impact on hyperscaler operating margins; 1 = elevated energy costs (linked to Hormuz or other supply shock) raising PUE-adjusted opex by >10% YoY for major data-center operators; 2 = energy costs structurally impair AI capex economics or trigger capex guidance cuts citing power costs

us-iran-conflict-triggers-new-energy-cos.rationale: s8_ai_capex tracks the circular financing risk of AI buildout (IG OAS, capex-vs-revenue gap, GPU-backed debt), but has no indicator for the energy-cost channel. The Hormuz shock created a sustained global energy-price elevation through H1 2026 that directly increases the operating expenditure of power-intensive AI infrastructure. This is a cross-story contagion (s20→s8 and s15) that is material but currently invisible to the tracker. The RBA's March 2026 FSR explicitly flags AI investment and energy market disruptions as co-occurring stressors.

boj-holds-at-1-0-10-year-jgb-at-2-78-jap.headline: BOJ Holds at 1.0%, 10-Year JGB at ~2.78%; Japanese Investors Sold $29.6bn US Treasuries in Q1 2026
boj-holds-at-1-0-10-year-jgb-at-2-78-jap.summary: The Bank of Japan held its policy rate at 1.0% on August 1 (passing 8-1 with one dissenter calling for 1.25%), while the 10-year JGB yield hovers near 2.78%—over 70bps higher YTD—and Tokyo suspected of FX intervention to support the yen. A new BOJ review published August 4 examines market impact of its ongoing JGB purchase reductions, a critical watch item as Japanese investors shed $29.6bn of US Treasuries in Q1 2026 alone.

proposed_indicator.label: Japanese net sales of foreign bonds (US Treasuries, $bn rolling 4-quarter)
proposed_indicator.rubric: Measures repatriation flow as domestic JGB yields rise. Sources: Japan MOF quarterly TIC-equivalent data. Threshold: <$20bn/yr = 0 ok; $20-60bn/yr = 1 elevated; >$60bn/yr = 2 disorderly (removes a structural buyer from UST market, amplifying basis-trade and fiscal risks).

boj-holds-at-1-0-10-year-jgb-at-2-78-jap.rationale: The existing s2_japan story tracks USD/JPY, 30yr JGB yield, and Takaichi financing clarity, but has no indicator capturing the capital-flow feedback loop: as domestic JGB yields become attractive at 2.78%+, Japanese life insurers and pension funds repatriate foreign bond holdings, withdrawing a historically reliable marginal buyer from the US Treasury market. At $29.6bn in Q1 alone, this is on pace for ~$120bn/yr—a quantity large enough to materially tighten UST supply/demand and interact with s1_basis_trade. This gap is material and distinct from existing indicators.

global-oil-demand-fell-5-mb-d-yoy-in-q2-.headline: Global Oil Demand Fell ~5 mb/d YoY in Q2 2026 on Hormuz Shock; IEA Coordinated 400mn-Barrel SPR Release
global-oil-demand-fell-5-mb-d-yoy-in-q2-.summary: Per IEA data cited by multiple sources this week, global oil demand in Q2 2026 fell by nearly 5 mb/d year-on-year as the Hormuz closure rippled through supply chains, forcing the IEA's 32 members to coordinate a release of over 400 million barrels from strategic petroleum reserves—one of the largest ever. China drew heavily on its estimated 1.5bn-barrel stockpile rather than competing for spot barrels.

proposed_indicator.label: IEA strategic reserve buffer remaining (% of full 90-day import cover)
proposed_indicator.rubric: Tracks IEA collective strategic petroleum reserve (SPR) adequacy after drawdowns. 0 = >80% cover (adequate); 1 = 60-80% cover (depleted, limited headroom for further shock); 2 = <60% cover (critically low, next supply shock would hit prices immediately). Sources: IEA Monthly Oil Market Report, US DOE SPR inventory levels, IEA member state submissions. After ~400mn-barrel coordinated release in 2026, this buffer deserves explicit tracking.

global-oil-demand-fell-5-mb-d-yoy-in-q2-.rationale: s20_sea_lanes currently tracks Hormuz status, WTI price, and cable incidents, but has no indicator for the 'insurance stock' of the global emergency response system. After the largest coordinated SPR release in history (400mn+ barrels), the ability to buffer a future supply shock is materially degraded. If the Hormuz interim deal collapses or a new shock hits before reserves are rebuilt, the price response would be far more severe than during the initial February shock. This gap is directly relevant to s18_food_fertilizer and s4_dev_debt as well.

houthi-blockade-of-bab-al-mandeb-closes-.headline: Houthi Blockade of Bab al-Mandeb Closes Saudi Arabia's Last Major Oil Export Corridor
houthi-blockade-of-bab-al-mandeb-closes-.summary: In July 2026 the Houthis declared a naval blockade of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait for Saudi-linked shipping, foiling Saudi Arabia's Hormuz bypass via the Yanbu Red Sea terminal. As of August 5–6, tanker attacks are ongoing, an Indian-flagged vessel sank, and Wood Mackenzie warns the 'sharp decline in Red Sea exports removes one of the Kingdom's few remaining sources of export options.'

proposed_indicator.label: Bab al-Mandeb / Saudi Red Sea corridor status (0 open / 1 contested / 2 blocked)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = normal Saudi tanker transit; 1 = partial Houthi interdiction / elevated attacks; 2 = declared blockade in force with tanker sinkings and Saudi export halt. Current reading: 2.

houthi-blockade-of-bab-al-mandeb-closes-.rationale: The existing s20_sea_lanes story tracks Hormuz/Red Sea status as a single composite indicator but the Bab al-Mandeb blockade is now a structurally distinct, additive closure: Hormuz is ~90% shut and Bab al-Mandeb is now also contested, together potentially blocking ~25% of global seaborne oil supply. The current single 'Hormuz/Red Sea status' indicator cannot capture the compounding dual-chokepoint risk or Saudi Arabia's loss of its last major bypass route. A dedicated indicator is warranted.

japan-30-year-jgb-yield-at-3-99-usd-jpy-.headline: Japan 30-Year JGB Yield at 3.99%; USD/JPY Decouples from Rate Differentials as Yen Enters New Fiscal-Risk Regime
japan-30-year-jgb-yield-at-3-99-usd-jpy-.summary: Japan's 30-year JGB yield held at 3.99% on August 3, up 87bps year-on-year, while Apollo Global Management published analysis (dated ~August 3) arguing USD/JPY has since April 2025 decoupled from rate differentials and is now driven by fiscal credibility and trade-war concerns—a structural shift that raises carry-trade unwind risk independent of BoJ policy moves.

proposed_indicator.label: USD/JPY vs. US-Japan 10y spread decoupling flag (0 coupled / 1 mild decoupling / 2 structural decoupling)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = USD/JPY moves within ±10% of what rate-differential model predicts; 1 = persistent divergence, fiscal/trade premium emerging; 2 = structural regime shift confirmed by multiple sell-side/central bank analyses with spread <2pp yet yen not strengthening. Current reading: 2, per Apollo analysis citing USD/JPY near 160 with spread ~2pp.

japan-30-year-jgb-yield-at-3-99-usd-jpy-.rationale: s2_japan already tracks USD/JPY and the 30-year JGB yield, but neither indicator captures the qualitative regime shift—that carry-trade risk is now driven by fiscal credibility rather than rate differentials alone. A decoupling indicator would flag when the standard hedging/carry logic breaks down, which is precisely when disorderly unwind risk is highest and the existing indicators could give false comfort.

us-fiscal-2026-deficit-projected-at-1-89.headline: US Fiscal 2026 Deficit Projected at $1.89 Trillion (5.9% GDP); OBBBA + Iran War Spending Compound Sovereign Financing Risk
us-fiscal-2026-deficit-projected-at-1-89.summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management estimates the FY2026 federal deficit at ~$1.89 trillion (5.9% of GDP), with federal debt rising to $32.2 trillion (100.4% of GDP). The CBO's February 2026 baseline predated Iran war defense expenditures, and court challenges to tariff revenue add further upside deficit risk—compounding Treasury supply pressure at a time of stressed foreign demand.

proposed_story.name: US Fiscal Dominance & Treasury Supply Overhang
proposed_story.why: The combination of OBBBA tax cuts (~$5 trillion over 10 years per Tax Foundation), unbudgeted Iran war spending, potential tariff revenue loss via court rulings, and federal debt crossing 100% of GDP in FY2026 creates a structural Treasury supply overhang. This is distinct from s1_basis_trade (which tracks leverage/clearing mechanics) and s4_dev_debt (which tracks EM sovereigns): this story concerns the US sovereign's own financing credibility, term-premium inflation, and the risk of fiscal dominance crowding out Fed independence—a scenario the RBA's March 2026 FSR and multiple sell-side analysts have flagged as a primary 2026 tail risk.

indicators.label: US 10-year Treasury term premium (ACM model, bps)
indicators.rubric: Rising term premium signals market demanding compensation for fiscal/supply risk. Watch for sustained move above 100bps ACM estimate as warning level; above 150bps as stress.

indicators.label: FY2026 US federal deficit vs. CBO baseline ($ bn deviation)
indicators.rubric: Tracks realized deficit versus CBO Feb-2026 baseline ($1.89T). Positive deviation = worse-than-expected. Iran war supplementals, tariff court rulings, and OBBBA permanent extension are key upside drivers.

indicators.label: Foreign official Treasury demand (% of gross issuance, TIC data)
indicators.rubric: Declining foreign official share of auction take-up at a time of record issuance signals forced domestic absorption at higher yields. Watch for sustained <15% foreign official share as stress threshold.

us-fiscal-2026-deficit-projected-at-1-89.rationale: No existing story explicitly tracks US sovereign fiscal credibility and the supply/demand imbalance in Treasury markets as a standalone risk. The OBBBA, Iran war supplementals, and potential tariff revenue shortfalls have materially degraded the US fiscal trajectory within the last 7 days' analytical cycle (updated J.P. Morgan and Econbrowser estimates), and the BoJ's reduced JGB purchase programme (s2) reduces one of the largest marginal buyers of Treasuries simultaneously. This confluence creates a new systemic story warranting dedicated monitoring.

usd-jpy-decoupled-from-rate-differential.headline: USD/JPY decoupled from rate differentials since April 2025: yen remains weak at ~155–156 despite JGB yield surge, signalling carry-trade overhang not yet unwound
usd-jpy-decoupled-from-rate-differential.summary: Apollo Global Management and Idea Farm analysis published within the past week show that USD/JPY has broken its historical relationship with US-Japan yield differentials since April 2025—the gap has narrowed toward 2 percentage points yet the yen trades near 155–156, suggesting a large residual carry-trade overhang. This decoupling means a disorderly unwind could be more violent than yield-spread models would predict, and no existing indicator captures this regime-shift risk.

proposed_indicator.label: USD/JPY vs. US-JP 10y yield-spread decoupling flag
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = USD/JPY within 5 yen of what the yield differential model predicts (coupled); 1 = 5–15 yen overvalued vs. model (partial decoupling, carry overhang building); 2 = >15 yen overvalued (severe decoupling, large latent carry unwind risk). Current: ~1 (yen ~155 vs. model-implied ~140–145 given 2pp spread).

usd-jpy-decoupled-from-rate-differential.rationale: The existing s2_japan tracker captures USD/JPY as a level indicator (yen strengthening = lower = risk) but does not capture the regime-shift risk identified by Apollo: the yen has stopped responding to yield-spread compression, implying a large undisclosed carry overhang that, when it unwinds, could be disproportionately violent. StoneX (May 2026) and Apollo/Idea Farm (Aug 3, 2026) both flag this as a distinct and growing risk requiring its own monitoring metric beyond a simple spot-rate watch.

simultaneous-hormuz-red-sea-dual-chokepo.headline: Simultaneous Hormuz + Red Sea dual-chokepoint closure: both of the Middle East's major sea lanes disrupted concurrently, Red Sea at 49% capacity, Hormuz at ~2% — no existing story captures compound supply-chain rupture
simultaneous-hormuz-red-sea-dual-chokepo.summary: Since late February 2026 when US/Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the Hormuz closure, both the Strait of Hormuz (effectively shut, ~2 transits/day vs. 73–130 normal) and the Red Sea route (operating at 49% of pre-crisis capacity after Houthis reversed October 2025 ceasefire gains) have been simultaneously disrupted — the worst dual maritime chokepoint crisis in modern history per Carra Globe. While s20_sea_lanes tracks Hormuz and s18_food_fertilizer captures fertilizer input risk, no existing story tracks the compound, self-reinforcing pressure on global shipping costs, energy supply, and food/fertilizer routing that arises specifically from both corridors being blocked simultaneously.

proposed_story.name: Dual maritime chokepoint rupture (Hormuz + Red Sea simultaneous closure)
proposed_story.why: The concurrent effective closure of both the Strait of Hormuz (~20% of world oil and LNG per Carra Globe) and the Red Sea corridor (49% capacity, serving Europe-Asia trade) creates a non-linear supply shock that is qualitatively different from either disruption alone: shipping costs, insurance premia, and rerouting costs compound across energy, food, fertilizer, and manufactured goods simultaneously. The existing s20_sea_lanes story tracks Hormuz status and WTI price but was designed for a single-chokepoint frame; it does not capture the systemic feedback loop between the two disruptions, the ~22,500 stranded mariners, or the broader macroeconomic inflation/stagflation channel from dual closure.

indicators.label: Dual-chokepoint combined throughput index (% of combined pre-crisis baseline)
indicators.rubric: Weighted average of (Hormuz daily transits / 100-vessel baseline) and (Red Sea weekly container throughput / pre-crisis baseline), expressed as %. Current: ~15–20% (Hormuz ~2%, Red Sea ~49%). 0–40% = acute dual closure; 40–70% = partial recovery; >70% = effective normalization.

indicators.label: Global container spot-rate index (Drewry WCI or Freightos FBX, USD/40ft)
indicators.rubric: Tracks shipping cost inflation from rerouting. Baseline (pre-2024): ~$1,500–2,000. Elevated: $4,000–6,000. Acute: >$6,000. Current: monitor weekly via Drewry World Container Index.

indicators.label: War-risk insurance premium for Persian Gulf transits (% of cargo value)
indicators.rubric: 0 = normal (<0.1% of cargo value); 1 = elevated (0.1–1.0%); 2 = prohibitive (>1.0% or Lloyd's market suspension of cover). Tracks financial-market read-through of physical risk.

indicators.label: Stranded-vessel / mariner count (vessels + persons)
indicators.rubric: Humanitarian and operational stress proxy. Carra Globe (May 2026 data): ~1,550 vessels, ~22,500 mariners. Tracks whether the crisis is deepening or resolving in physical terms independent of diplomatic signals.

simultaneous-hormuz-red-sea-dual-chokepo.rationale: At level 8/10, this is the single highest-materiality new development of the past week. The Carra Globe tracker (updated July 30 / Aug 2026) confirms the strait is effectively closed with only ~2 transits/day, the June MoU broke down in early July after vessel attacks, and the Red Sea simultaneously operates at 49% capacity after Houthis reversed ceasefire gains. Treasury Secretary Bessent's Aug 4 comment about a deal 'in the next two days' (Washington Times) has not materialized as of Aug 7, and Iran's precondition (US lifting its port blockade) remains unmet per CNN Aug 5. The dual-chokepoint frame belongs in Set 4 (alongside s19_lithography and s20_sea_lanes) as a geopolitical-physical chokepoint story, but it requires its own story entry because the compound effect on global shipping, energy, food, and fertilizer supply chains is materially larger than either single-corridor disruption captured in the existing tracker.

china-extends-rare-earth-entity-bans-to-.headline: China Extends Rare-Earth Entity Bans to 14 EU Firms — No Existing Indicator Captures Third-Country Export Restrictions
china-extends-rare-earth-entity-bans-to-.summary: On 24 July 2026, China's Ministry of Commerce blocked dual-use rare-earth and critical-mineral shipments to 14 firms across the European Union, a geographic expansion of entity-specific controls beyond the US that falls outside the current s6_rare_earths indicator set, which only tracks a US domestic producer blacklist.

proposed_indicator.label: Ex-US third-country RE entity bans (0 none / 1 isolated-country bans / 2 multi-region bans)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = no bans on non-US allies; 1 = entity-specific bans in one allied jurisdiction (e.g. EU or Japan); 2 = simultaneous entity bans across two or more allied jurisdictions, signalling systemic weaponisation beyond bilateral US-China dispute

china-extends-rare-earth-entity-bans-to-.rationale: The existing s6 blacklist indicator is US-centric. The EU entity bans represent a qualitatively different escalation — China is now using mineral controls as leverage against multiple Western blocs simultaneously. As the November 2026 pause expiry approaches, this third-country dimension could accelerate alternative supply-chain investments or retaliatory trade measures and needs its own indicator to track geographic spread.

hormuz-closure-triggers-systemic-fertili.headline: Hormuz Closure Triggers Systemic Fertilizer & LNG Input Shock — A New Compounding Risk Across s18 and s20
hormuz-closure-triggers-systemic-fertili.summary: The protracted Hormuz closure has pushed combined export volumes of fertilizers, chemicals, plastics, and aluminium down sharply alongside energy, with LNG from Qatar's Ras Laffan (force majeure declared March 2026) still not fully recovered. The UN ITC finds alternative suppliers have only fully offset Hormuz shortfalls for ammonia and polypropylene, leaving food-input supply chains materially short.

proposed_indicator.label: Non-energy Hormuz commodity substitution gap (0 fully offset / 1 partial offset / 2 structural shortfall)
proposed_indicator.rubric: Tracks UN ITC / IEA assessments of whether alternative suppliers have fully replaced Hormuz-route volumes for fertilizer inputs (ammonia, urea, sulphur), petrochemical feedstocks, and aluminium. 0 = all major products fully substituted; 1 = substitution partial, inventories drawing down; 2 = two or more critical non-energy commodities in structural shortfall with no near-term alternative, implying food/manufacturing cost pass-through.

hormuz-closure-triggers-systemic-fertili.rationale: The existing s18 indicator 'Hormuz/Gulf disruption to fertilizer inputs' only uses a binary open/disrupted/cut rubric tied to the Hormuz status. The UN ITC's August 5 finding that only 2 of 12 product categories have been fully substituted reveals a more granular, multi-commodity substitution failure. A dedicated substitution-gap indicator would let the tracker distinguish between the strait being 'contested' (s20) and the downstream commodity supply actually being replenished — a critical nuance for food and industrial risk assessment.

japan-30-year-jgb-yield-hits-3-96-august.headline: Japan 30-year JGB yield hits 3.96% (August 10) as Japan directly intervenes in yen; carry-trade migration to EUR/CHF funding limits contagion but does not eliminate it
japan-30-year-jgb-yield-hits-3-96-august.summary: Japan's 30-year JGB yield rose to 3.96% on August 10, up 88bp year-on-year, while the 10-year reached 2.81%. Japan conducted direct FX intervention to support the yen; the Bloomberg EM Carry Index fell only ~1% (vs 4% in August 2024), as investors have shifted funding to euros and Swiss francs, partially defusing near-term systemic risk.

proposed_indicator.label: Japan FX intervention frequency (rolling 30-day count of MoF/BOJ confirmed interventions)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = no intervention in 30 days; 1 = 1–2 interventions (verbal or limited); 2 = 3+ interventions or multi-billion direct action

japan-30-year-jgb-yield-hits-3-96-august.rationale: The existing s2_japan story tracks USD/JPY and the 30-year JGB yield — both are flashing amber (3.96% 30yr, yen under pressure despite intervention). However, no existing indicator captures the *frequency and scale of MoF/BOJ direct FX interventions*, which is the novel August 2026 development. Intervention frequency is a leading stress gauge: repeated actions signal the BOJ is losing the battle to contain yen weakness passively. The muted carry-index response (only –1%) is noteworthy but the shift of funding to EUR/CHF is a structural change worth tracking separately.

china-activates-enforcement-teeth-on-rar.headline: China activates enforcement teeth on rare-earth controls: foreign nationals detained in Dalian, Chinese exec arrested for germanium smuggling
china-activates-enforcement-teeth-on-rar.summary: Morgan Lewis (July 2026) confirmed that two Japanese nationals were detained in Dalian in May 2026 for alleged rare-earth smuggling, the first known foreign-national detention under China's export-control framework. Separately, a Chinese optics company chairman was arrested in June 2026 for falsely declaring germanium-containing lenses to circumvent export licenses. MOFCOM Announcement No. 26 of 2026 formalised a public reporting mechanism for violations, signalling systematic enforcement escalation ahead of the November 10, 2026 expiry of the Oct-2025 rare-earth control pause.

proposed_indicator.label: China RE enforcement actions (detentions, prosecutions, MOFCOM violation disclosures, rolling 90-day count)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = none; 1 = 1–2 isolated cases (company-level fines or warnings); 2 = foreign-national detentions, criminal prosecutions, or sector-wide compliance sweeps

china-activates-enforcement-teeth-on-rar.rationale: The s6_rare_earths story tracks export-license flow and the Nov-2025 pause status, but has no indicator for *enforcement intensity*. The arrest of foreign nationals and Chinese executives for circumventing controls is qualitatively new: it signals Beijing is hardening the administrative architecture regardless of the diplomatic pause, and creates compliance chilling effects on downstream manufacturers. With the pause expiring November 10, 2026, enforcement escalation now serves as a leading indicator of what the post-pause regime will look like. This is a story_gap because the materiality is high but no existing indicator captures it.

hormuz-driven-energy-shock-triggers-larg.headline: Hormuz-driven energy shock triggers largest oil supply disruption in history: OPEC output down 30%+, IEA releases 400 million barrels of strategic reserves
hormuz-driven-energy-shock-triggers-larg.summary: The Brookings Institution and IEA confirm that OPEC production has fallen more than 30% since the February 28, 2026 outbreak of the US-Israel-Iran conflict, with Hormuz ship traffic at near-standstill. The IEA declared this the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market and coordinated a 400-million-barrel strategic-reserve release — now effectively exhausted as collateral.

proposed_story.name: Strategic petroleum reserve (SPR) depletion & oil-shock macro pass-through
proposed_story.why: The Iran war has triggered the largest oil supply disruption in recorded history, with a coordinated 400-million-barrel SPR release now largely deployed. Once strategic buffers are exhausted, the next supply shock — or prolonged Hormuz closure — hits market prices directly with no policy cushion. This creates a distinct second-order risk not captured by s20_sea_lanes (which tracks the shipping-lane status) or s18_food_fertilizer (fertilizer inputs): the depletion of the global SPR buffer itself is a macro-financial stress vector driving inflation, sovereign energy import bills, EM currency pressure, and potentially forcing central banks to choose between fighting inflation and supporting growth.

indicators.label: IEA / US SPR days-of-import cover (days)
indicators.rubric: Current cover vs. 90-day IEA target; >90 = green, 60–90 = amber, <60 = red

indicators.label: Brent crude spot (USD/bbl)
indicators.rubric: Price level: <$80 = easing, $80–100 = elevated, >$100 = acute

indicators.label: G7/IEA coordinated SPR release status (0 available / 1 partially deployed / 2 exhausted)
indicators.rubric: 0 = reserves intact and available for deployment; 1 = partial release underway; 2 = cumulative releases exceed IEA-estimated usable buffer (~1.4bn bbl across IEA members)

hormuz-driven-energy-shock-triggers-larg.rationale: The existing tracker captures s20_sea_lanes (Hormuz status, WTI price, cable incidents) and s18_food_fertilizer (Hormuz disruption to fertilizer inputs). Neither story covers the *depletion of the SPR buffer as a systemic macro risk*. With 400 million barrels already released — the largest coordinated draw in IEA history — the world is materially closer to a state where a second disruption or prolonged closure produces unmitigated price spikes. This is a distinct, traceable risk with its own indicators (days-of-cover, Brent, SPR status) and warrants a new story at proposed level 8 given the potential for global stagflation, EM balance-of-payment crises, and central bank policy dilemmas.

japan-us-coordinated-fx-intervention-jul.headline: Japan–US coordinated FX intervention July 31: structural yen weakness unresolved as BOJ faces fiscal-monetary trilemma
japan-us-coordinated-fx-intervention-jul.summary: The US Treasury and Japan's Finance Ministry conducted a joint yen-buying, euro-selling intervention on July 31 — the first US-assisted yen intervention in decades — after USD/JPY fell to 40-year lows; Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly confirmed it on August 3. Analysts at MUFG and Investing.com note the intervention has not resolved the underlying drivers (rate gap, fiscal risk, import inflation), and markets still assign a high probability of a BoJ rate hike in September, which would further raise Japan's debt-servicing cost against a backdrop of the Takaichi tax cut.

proposed_indicator.label: US-Japan coordinated FX intervention flag (0 none / 1 unilateral BoJ / 2 joint US-Japan)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = no intervention; 1 = BoJ acting alone (standard); 2 = joint US Treasury + BoJ intervention signaling systemic yen stress. Current reading: 2. Reset to 1 when joint action ceases; to 0 after 90 days of market stability.

japan-us-coordinated-fx-intervention-jul.rationale: s2_japan tracks USD/JPY as a value indicator but has no binary flag for the qualitative escalation of a coordinated US-Japan intervention — a rare event last seen in 1998 and 2011. Joint intervention signals that yen weakness has crossed a threshold of systemic concern for both sovereigns, creating a distinct macro signal beyond the spot rate itself. Without this flag, the tracker cannot distinguish between routine yen drift and a structural crisis requiring cross-border policy coordination.

obbba-enacted-us-debt-to-gdp-projected-t.headline: OBBBA enacted: US debt-to-GDP projected to hit 120–129% by mid-2030s; FY2026 deficit at $1.4tn through June; next debt ceiling breach ~2027
obbba-enacted-us-debt-to-gdp-projected-t.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act raised the statutory debt ceiling to $41.1 trillion (+$5tn) and is projected by CBO to add $3.4tn to primary deficits over ten years, with CRFB estimating debt at 120% of GDP by FY2035 under conservative assumptions and 134% if tariff revenue falls short and temporary provisions are made permanent. The federal deficit for FY2026 reached $1.4tn through June, and BPC projects the new ceiling will be breached again in late winter–mid-summer 2027.

proposed_story.name: US sovereign fiscal trajectory / Treasury supply shock
proposed_story.why: The OBBBA structurally raises US borrowing needs by $3.4–5.5tn over the decade, with the next debt-ceiling breach expected in 2027. This creates a persistent Treasury supply overhang that interacts with at least four existing tracker stories (s1_basis_trade via MOVE and SOFR; s7_stablecoins via stablecoin Treasury demand; s12_gold_dedollar via USD reserve share; s4_dev_debt via global risk-free rate). It is distinct from all existing stories: s1 covers hidden leverage, not sovereign issuance dynamics; s4 covers developing-world debt, not the US itself; s12 covers de-dollarization drivers, not the primary supply-side cause. A dedicated story is warranted given the multi-year, structural, market-moving nature of the development.

indicators.label: US federal deficit (% of GDP, trailing 12 months)
indicators.rubric: Current ~6.0% of GDP. Threshold: >5% elevated / >7% severe. Sources: BPC Deficit Tracker (monthly), CBO.

indicators.label: US 10-year Treasury term premium (ACM model, bps)
indicators.rubric: Tracks investor demand compensation for fiscal risk. Rising term premium (>80bps) signals market is pricing sovereign supply risk. Source: NY Fed ACM daily.

indicators.label: Treasury auction tail / primary dealer absorption rate (0 normal / 1 elevated / 2 systemic)
indicators.rubric: 0 = primary dealers absorb <15% of auction; 1 = 15–25% (March 2026 episode: 24% of 2-yr); 2 = >25% or failed auction. Source: TreasuryDirect, BPC auction tracker.

obbba-enacted-us-debt-to-gdp-projected-t.rationale: No existing tracker story captures the US sovereign as the risk entity. The OBBBA's enactment in 2025 and its now-visible fiscal math (debt at $39.6tn currently, ceiling breach 2027, deficit $1.4tn through June 2026) represents a new structural supply-of-safe-assets shock with direct read-through to Treasury volatility (MOVE), carry-trade funding costs, and the de-dollarization narrative. The BPC already documented weak Treasury auctions in March 2026 (primary dealers absorbing 24% of 2-yr note), which is a near-activation of the basis-trade amplifier. A standalone story is needed to track this upstream risk.

boj-september-rate-hike-now-priced-at-78.headline: BOJ September Rate Hike Now Priced at 78%; 30-Year JGB Yield Approaches 4% as Japan-US Jointly Intervene in FX
boj-september-rate-hike-now-priced-at-78.summary: As of August 12, markets price a 78% probability of a BOJ rate hike at the September meeting (up sharply from 66% on Monday), driven by hawkish July meeting minutes and persistent yen weakness amplifying oil-driven inflation. The 30-year JGB yield is at 3.990% and the 10-year at 2.84%, with Japan-US joint FX intervention recently deployed to support the yen.

proposed_indicator.label: BOJ September hike probability (%, market-implied)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0–30% = low pressure (0); 31–65% = rising pressure (1); >65% = imminent hike risk (2). Currently ~78% → level 2. Source: Tokyo Tanshi OIS pricing, Bloomberg.

boj-september-rate-hike-now-priced-at-78.rationale: The existing s2_japan story tracks the 30-year JGB yield and USD/JPY but has no indicator capturing the imminent policy catalyst — the probability of the September BOJ hike. At 78% and climbing, this is the key trigger for carry-trade unwind acceleration and a material gap in the tracker. Joint Japan-US FX intervention is also a new development not captured by existing indicators. The 30-year JGB yield at 3.990% should also be updated (existing indicator).

qatar-lng-infrastructure-damage-delays-g.headline: Qatar LNG Infrastructure Damage Delays Global LNG Supply Wave by Years; Europe Faces Costly US LNG Dependency
qatar-lng-infrastructure-damage-delays-g.summary: The IEA estimates damage to Qatari LNG liquefaction infrastructure from the Middle East conflict will remove ~140 billion cubic metres of LNG supply between 2026–2030, with the anticipated global LNG supply wave materially delayed. If Qatari disruptions persist, the US could supply two-thirds of Europe's LNG imports in 2026 at significantly higher cost.

proposed_story.name: LNG supply shock — Qatar infrastructure damage & European energy dependency
proposed_story.why: The Middle East conflict has structurally damaged Qatari LNG liquefaction capacity, removing an estimated 140 bcm of supply through 2030 and forcing Europe into a higher-cost, politically fragile dependency on US LNG. This is distinct from the Hormuz/Red Sea sea-lane story (s20) — it is about permanent or multi-year infrastructure destruction affecting the medium-term global gas market, European industrial competitiveness, and EM energy-import solvency. It also interacts with s18_food_fertilizer (nitrogen fertilizer uses gas feedstock) and s10_france (European energy cost pass-through to already-fragile fiscal positions).

indicators.label: Qatar LNG export capacity utilization (% of pre-conflict baseline)
indicators.rubric: >85% = recovering (0); 60–85% = impaired (1); <60% = severely disrupted (2). Current estimate: ~50–60% → level 2. Source: IEA Gas Market Report, S&P Global Platts.

indicators.label: European spot TTF gas price (EUR/MWh)
indicators.rubric: Track absolute level; >80 EUR/MWh = elevated stress; >120 EUR/MWh = acute. Source: ICE TTF front-month.

indicators.label: IEA cumulative LNG supply loss estimate 2026-2030 (bcm)
indicators.rubric: Track IEA quarterly Gas Market Report revisions. Current: ~140 bcm loss. Upward revision = worsening.

qatar-lng-infrastructure-damage-delays-g.rationale: No existing story covers medium-term structural LNG supply destruction — s20_sea_lanes tracks transit disruptions (open/contested/closed) but not permanent capacity impairment. The 140 bcm IEA estimate and Europe's forced pivot to expensive US LNG represent a multi-year macro risk to European growth, inflation, and industrial competitiveness that warrants its own story node.

china-rare-earth-entity-bans-extended-to.headline: China Rare Earth Entity Bans Extended to 14 EU Firms in July 2026 — Escalating Beyond US Bilateral to Multilateral Weaponization
china-rare-earth-entity-bans-extended-to.summary: China expanded its dual-use rare earth export bans from 10 US companies (June 22) to 14 EU-linked defense and critical-mineral firms in July 2026, signaling a strategic broadening of mineral weaponization beyond the US-China bilateral axis to a wider Western-China technology rivalry.

proposed_indicator.label: Non-US allied entities on China dual-use RE export blacklist (count)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 entities = bilateral only (0); 1–20 entities = selective multilateral escalation (1); >20 entities or sector-wide allied ban = systemic (2). Current: ~14 EU firms → level 1. Source: China MOFCOM entity list updates, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.

china-rare-earth-entity-bans-extended-to.rationale: The existing s6_rare_earths indicators focus on US-centric metrics (US domestic producer blacklist, export license flow, ex-China price premium). The July expansion to EU firms is a qualitatively new dimension — China is now using RE export controls as multilateral economic coercion against a wider G7 coalition — not captured by any current indicator. Adding an 'allied entity count' indicator closes this gap and gives the tracker early warning of escalation from entity-specific to sector-wide Western bans.

historic-us-japan-joint-yen-intervention.headline: Historic US–Japan Joint Yen Intervention Fails to Hold — USD/JPY Rebounds to 159–160, Carry Shorts Rebuild
historic-us-japan-joint-yen-intervention.summary: The first bilateral US–Japan FX intervention since 1998 (confirmed August 3) drove USD/JPY from a 40-year high of ~164 to 156, but the yen has already retraced half its gains to ~159–160 by August 11–14, with Bloomberg reporting carry traders actively rebuilding yen short positions as of today. The BOJ policy rate remains at 0.75% and the interest-rate differential continues to incentivize carry, leaving the risk of a disorderly second-leg unwind elevated ahead of the September 18 BOJ meeting.

proposed_indicator.label: Joint FX intervention exhaustion / carry-rebuild signal
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = intervention holding (USD/JPY stable ≤158 post-action); 1 = partial retracement (158–161, carry rebuilding but orderly); 2 = full retracement / disorderly (>161, interventions exhausted, second-leg unwind risk acute)

historic-us-japan-joint-yen-intervention.rationale: s2_japan already tracks USD/JPY as a value indicator, but does not capture the qualitative state of bilateral intervention credibility — the key new variable. The failure of the first US–Japan joint action since 1998 to sustain yen strength, with carry traders explicitly rebuilding shorts as of today, represents a structurally new regime signal that goes beyond the spot rate itself. A band indicator on intervention exhaustion is needed to track whether the policy backstop is credible or has been arbitraged away.

strategic-petroleum-reserve-depletion-cr.headline: Strategic Petroleum Reserve Depletion Creates New 'Energy-Security Buffer' Risk with No Existing Tracker Indicator
strategic-petroleum-reserve-depletion-cr.summary: The US SPR has fallen below 300 million barrels for the first time since January 1983 following the historic 400-million-barrel IEA coordinated release (March 2026), leaving only ~172 days of theoretical cover at normal drawdown rates — and the IEA's August OMR now projects a Q3 deficit of 1.8 mb/d with Hormuz still effectively closed. No existing tracker indicator captures the remaining SPR/strategic buffer capacity as a standalone risk variable.

proposed_indicator.label: Strategic petroleum reserve adequacy (days of crisis cover remaining)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = adequate (US SPR >400 mb, IEA members >90 days net import cover); 1 = depleting (US SPR 300–400 mb or IEA aggregate cover 60–90 days); 2 = critically low (US SPR <300 mb or IEA aggregate cover <60 days — current reading as of Aug 2026)

strategic-petroleum-reserve-depletion-cr.rationale: s20_sea_lanes tracks Hormuz open/closed and WTI price, but has no indicator for how much emergency buffer remains to absorb a prolonged closure. With the SPR now below 300 mb for the first time in 43 years and the IEA 400 mb coordinated release providing only ~10 days of full replacement, the residual strategic buffer has become an independent second-order risk variable. If Hormuz remains closed beyond Q3, there is no historical precedent for the level of SPR depletion that would result, making this a material gap in the existing framework.

japanese-investors-sold-29-6-bn-of-us-tr.headline: Japanese investors sold $29.6 bn of US Treasuries in Q1 2026 alone as domestic yields attract repatriation
japanese-investors-sold-29-6-bn-of-us-tr.summary: Rising JGB yields are pulling Japanese capital home: investors offloaded $29.6 billion of US debt in Q1 2026, removing a historically reliable marginal buyer from a market already navigating large US fiscal deficits. This structural outflow compounds basis-trade leverage risk by thinning the non-dealer Treasury demand base.

proposed_indicator.label: Japanese net UST selling (rolling 4-quarter, $bn)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = net buying or neutral; negative values = net selling. Threshold: > $50bn annualised selling = elevated (1); > $100bn = stress (2). Directional shift matters as much as level.

japanese-investors-sold-29-6-bn-of-us-tr.rationale: The basis trade's hidden leverage story is primarily about dealer capacity and repo market stress, but a key amplifier is the marginal Treasury buyer. Japanese repatriation at this scale ($29.6bn in a single quarter) represents a structural demand withdrawal that no existing indicator in s1 captures. It also interacts with s12_gold_dedollar (de-dollarization) and s4_dev_debt (stronger USD pressure) making it a cross-story gap worth tracking explicitly.

japan-stagflation-trap-gdp-miss-30-year-.headline: Japan stagflation trap: GDP miss + 30-year JGB high signals new systemic stress scenario not fully captured by existing indicators
japan-stagflation-trap-gdp-miss-30-year-.summary: The simultaneous arrival of a 30-year JGB yield high (10-year at 2.93%) and a sharp Q2 GDP miss (1.1% annualised vs 2% forecast) creates a novel 'stagflation trap' for the BOJ: tightening to defend the yen/inflation anchor risks crashing growth; not tightening risks further carry-unwind. Neither the existing 30-year JGB yield indicator nor USD/JPY alone captures this policy-trap dimension, which is the key contagion transmission mechanism to global risk assets.

proposed_indicator.label: BOJ policy-trap score (0 = aligned / 1 = tension / 2 = dilemma)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = inflation and growth both allow BOJ to act consistently (either both hawkish or both dovish). 1 = mild tension between inflation mandate and growth outlook. 2 = acute dilemma: JGB yields at multi-decade highs AND GDP growth missing by >50bps annualised simultaneously, forcing BOJ into a no-good-option policy corner with direct carry-unwind contagion risk to global assets.

japan-stagflation-trap-gdp-miss-30-year-.rationale: The August 2024 precedent (BOJ hike + weak US jobs data = Nikkei -12% in one session, S&P -3%) shows the contagion path is real and fast. The current setup — 10-year JGB at 2.93% (30-year high), GDP at half the forecast, BOJ September hike still priced — is arguably more dangerous because fiscal pressures under PM Takaichi are larger, the yen carry trade is still extended, and US SPR buffers are depleted. A binary 'yield level' metric misses the policy-trap dynamic; a composite score would give earlier warning.

strait-of-hormuz-remains-effectively-con.headline: Strait of Hormuz remains effectively contested: fresh tanker attacks (Aug 14) push Brent to ~$89–90/bbl, EIA sees no full recovery before 2027
strait-of-hormuz-remains-effectively-con.summary: Two UAE ADNOC tankers were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 14, 2026, denting hopes of reopening; Brent rose >2% to ~$89–90/bbl (~24% above pre-conflict levels). The US EIA projected Middle East oil production will not return to near pre-conflict levels until early 2027 and expects Brent to average $87/bbl for 2026.
strait-of-hormuz-remains-effectively-con.target_indicator: Hormuz/Red Sea status (0 open / 1 contested / 2 closed) → update to 2 (effectively closed/contested); WTI crude (CL=F) → ~$82–83/bbl; Undersea cable incidents → 0
strait-of-hormuz-remains-effectively-con.rationale: Fresh tanker attacks on Aug 14 within the 7-day window directly update s20_sea_lanes' Hormuz status indicator. A prolonged near-closure of the world's largest oil chokepoint is materially affecting WTI/Brent, global inflation, and central bank policy paths simultaneously, and the EIA's 2027 recovery timeline signals this is not short-term noise.

japan-jgb-yields-at-30-year-highs-2-95-o.headline: Japan JGB yields at 30-year highs (~2.95% on 10y, targeting 3%); Takaichi food-tax cut cabinet-approved Aug 5 with BOJ ETF-tap trial balloon signalling fiscal-monetary boundary risk
japan-jgb-yields-at-30-year-highs-2-95-o.summary: Japan's 10-year JGB yield reached 2.95% on Aug 18 (highest since 1996), driven by BOJ rate-hike speculation for September and Takaichi's Aug 5 cabinet approval of a food sales-tax cut from 8% to 1% that creates a ~JPY 4.4 trillion/year funding gap. A senior LDP executive floated tapping BOJ ETF holdings to fund the gap, raising acute concerns about fiscal-monetary boundary erosion; Oxford Economics now targets 10y JGB at 3% by end-2026.

proposed_indicator.label: BOJ balance-sheet fiscal-use risk (0 none / 1 political pressure / 2 actual deployment)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = BOJ independence intact, no fiscal use of balance sheet discussed; 1 = ruling-party officials publicly float using BOJ ETF/JGB holdings to fund fiscal gap; 2 = BOJ formally directed or agrees to deploy balance-sheet assets for fiscal purposes

japan-jgb-yields-at-30-year-highs-2-95-o.rationale: The existing s2_japan story tracks JGB yields and Takaichi financing clarity, but the 'Takaichi plan financing clarity' indicator does not specifically capture the new and distinct risk that the BOJ's own balance sheet (ETF holdings accumulated during QE) could be politically commandeered to finance fiscal deficits. This would be a qualitative regime change for Japanese monetary credibility—different in kind from unclear debt issuance—warranting its own indicator. Current status: 1 (political pressure openly voiced by LDP insider).

japan-s-massive-ust-selling-continues-29.headline: Japan's massive UST selling continues: $29.6bn in Q1 2026 alone as rising domestic JGB yields incentivise repatriation, threatening a key marginal buyer of US Treasuries
japan-s-massive-ust-selling-continues-29.summary: With domestic JGB yields now at multi-decade highs, Japanese investors sold $29.6 billion of US Treasuries in Q1 2026 alone. As the BOJ contemplates further rate hikes and JGB yields approach 3%, the structural repatriation flow threatens one of the largest marginal buyers of US debt at a time when US fiscal deficits are near record levels.

proposed_indicator.label: Japanese institutional UST net selling (rolling 4-quarter, $bn, TIC data)
proposed_indicator.rubric: Track US Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for Japan net purchases/sales of long-term US Treasuries. Threshold: >$50bn annualised net selling = elevated; >$100bn = high risk (adds to basis-trade unwind pressure and term-premium spike risk). Source: US Treasury TIC monthly release.

japan-s-massive-ust-selling-continues-29.rationale: The s1_basis_trade story monitors Treasury market stress (MOVE, SOFR-EFFR, SEC clearing), but lacks an indicator tracking the structural demand side—specifically Japan's repatriation selling, which is now quantified and large (~$29.6bn in a single quarter). This is distinct from basis-trade leverage and directly affects UST term premia and auction dynamics. It could amplify any basis-trade unwind or clearing-market stress episode.

china-july-ppi-3-5-yoy-vs-4-1-prior-oil-.headline: China July PPI +3.5% YoY (vs +4.1% prior): oil-shock disinflationary fade revives deflation re-entry risk as domestic demand stays weak
china-july-ppi-3-5-yoy-vs-4-1-prior-oil-.summary: China's July 2026 PPI rose only 3.5% YoY versus 4.1% in June, the first deceleration since PPI turned positive in March 2026 on oil-shock pass-through; the Bloomberg report notes this is 'the first slowdown since China's PPI turned positive.' With domestic demand weak and the Hormuz oil shock fading, the risk of China reverting to PPI deflation—and exporting it globally via cheap manufactured goods—has materially re-escalated.
china-july-ppi-3-5-yoy-vs-4-1-prior-oil-.target_indicator: China PPI YoY (%) → update to +3.5% (July 2026, decelerating sharply from +4.1%); monitor direction: a continued deceleration toward 0% or below re-activates the deflationary spillover risk that was temporarily suppressed by the oil shock
china-july-ppi-3-5-yoy-vs-4-1-prior-oil-.rationale: The PPI figure is the primary quantitative indicator for s5_china_deflation. The July print is the most recent data point (within 7 days) and shows a meaningful directional reversal that warrants a tracker update. The Hormuz ceasefire negotiations—if concluded—would further remove the oil-shock prop, accelerating the PPI deceleration trajectory.

us-israel-iran-war-june-ceasefire-deal-f.headline: US-Israel-Iran war: June ceasefire/deal framework fragile; tanker attacks persist 5+ months after conflict began; LNG disruption (Qatar Ras Laffan halt) and fertilizer supply chain shock still reverberating
us-israel-iran-war-june-ceasefire-deal-f.summary: The US-Iran conflict that began Feb 28, 2026 produced a June MOU with a 60-day negotiating window for a final deal (including Hormuz reopening and $300bn Iran reconstruction fund), but new tanker attacks on Aug 14 demonstrate the ceasefire is not holding. Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG plant (world's largest) was temporarily halted earlier in the conflict; the CSIS notes that the Hormuz closure sharply increased sulfur/sulfuric acid prices, raising costs across critical mineral and fertilizer supply chains.

proposed_story.name: US-Israel-Iran War: Multi-vector macro shock (energy, LNG, fertilizer, nuclear proliferation, ceasefire fragility)
proposed_story.why: The February 2026 US-Israel strikes on Iran triggered a five-month-long Hormuz disruption affecting ~20% of global seaborne oil and LNG, a temporary Qatar LNG halt, spiking fertilizer input costs (sulfur/sulfuric acid), and persistent nuclear proliferation uncertainty. A June MOU opened a 60-day deal window but renewed tanker attacks on Aug 14 signal the ceasefire is not self-enforcing. This conflict is now the primary exogenous macro shock for 2026 and warrants its own story node, as its tentacles reach s20_sea_lanes, s18_food_fertilizer, s5_china_deflation, s16_copper (mineral supply chains), and global inflation/central bank paths simultaneously.

indicators.label: US-Iran ceasefire/deal durability (0 holding / 1 fragile / 2 collapsed)
indicators.rubric: 0 = 60-day negotiating framework on track, no major violations; 1 = sporadic attacks or negotiation setbacks, framework at risk; 2 = formal breakdown, renewed large-scale hostilities, or Iranian nuclear escalation

indicators.label: Brent crude (USD/bbl, ICE BRN=F) – war-premium proxy
indicators.rubric: Current: ~$88–90. Threshold bands: <$80 = war premium fading; $80–95 = elevated/contested; >$95 = acute shortage/escalation premium

indicators.label: Iran nuclear breakout risk (0 no change / 1 enrichment uptick / 2 weaponisation signal)
indicators.rubric: 0 = IAEA monitoring intact, enrichment frozen per MOU; 1 = enrichment activity increase detected or IAEA access limited; 2 = 90%+ enrichment confirmed or nuclear device assembly indicators

indicators.label: Middle East LNG/fertilizer supply disruption (0 normal / 1 partial / 2 acute)
indicators.rubric: 0 = Qatar Ras Laffan and Gulf LNG/sulfur flows fully restored; 1 = partial disruption, elevated spot prices; 2 = major LNG plant offline or Hormuz-linked fertilizer input shortage causing food-price spikes

us-israel-iran-war-june-ceasefire-deal-f.rationale: No existing story in the tracker captures the US-Israel-Iran conflict as a unified risk node. While s20_sea_lanes tracks Hormuz/WTI and s18_food_fertilizer tracks fertilizer inputs, the conflict simultaneously drives nuclear proliferation risk, LNG disruption, oil-price-mediated global inflation, ceasefire fragility, and critical mineral supply chain cost shocks through a single geopolitical driver. A dedicated story with a proposed_level of 9/10 (highest active macro shock in the system) is warranted to track these interlinked dimensions holistically and avoid indicator fragmentation across five separate existing stories.

boj-september-rate-hike-expectations-int.headline: BOJ September rate-hike expectations intensify: 10y JGB at 2.95% (Aug 18), Japanese PPI +7.2% YoY in July; domestic capital repatriation and yen dynamics create carry-unwind risk
boj-september-rate-hike-expectations-int.summary: Japan's 10-year JGB yield hit 2.95% on August 18, 2026 (the highest since 1996), with markets pricing a near-certain BOJ rate hike for September after multiple policymakers called for a stronger inflation response; July PPI rose 7.2% YoY partly due to Middle East oil costs. The confluence of imminent BOJ hikes, Takaichi fiscal expansion, and USD/JPY dynamics has materially elevated carry-trade unwind risk that was last acute in August 2024.
boj-september-rate-hike-expectations-int.target_indicator: 30-year JGB yield (%) → estimated ~3.6–3.7% range based on curve; USD/JPY → monitor for yen strengthening on BOJ hike; Takaichi plan financing clarity → update to 2 (disorderly, given BOJ ETF-tap trial balloon and unclear debt-offset mechanism per HSBC/Oxford Economics)
boj-september-rate-hike-expectations-int.rationale: Multiple current s2_japan indicators are simultaneously flashing. The 10y JGB at 2.95% (approaching Oxford Economics' 3% year-end target), the BOJ September hike probability rising sharply, and the Takaichi food-tax-cut financing opacity (now with BOJ ETF suggestion) collectively move the 'Takaichi plan financing clarity' indicator from 1 (unclear) to 2 (disorderly). The 30y JGB yield is likely in the 3.6–3.7% range (extrapolating from the curve structure seen in data). This is a high-materiality update to existing story indicators.

france-bayrou-government-faces-september.headline: France Bayrou government faces September 8 no-confidence vote; OAT-Bund spread widens toward 77-80 bp
france-bayrou-government-faces-september.summary: French PM François Bayrou announced on August 25 a no-confidence vote for September 8, triggering a market correction: the OAT-Bund 10-year spread widened from ~65 bp on August 15 to ~77 bp by August 25, with analysts at ABN AMRO targeting 85 bp by year-end. France's 2026 budget deficit is tracking near 5% of GDP — well above government targets — and public debt is projected to exceed 125% of GDP by 2030.
france-bayrou-government-faces-september.rationale: A scheduled no-confidence vote on September 8 moves the 'Govt stability' indicator to '2 = collapse-or-snap-election'. The OAT-Bund spread widening to 77 bp (from 65 bp in mid-August) is a direct update to the spread indicator. The story is escalating: credit agencies have already begun downgrading France, the deficit is tracking well above target, and a change in PM could produce looser fiscal policy (Citi flags far-right or left coalition would reverse pension reform). The rating action indicator may move from '1 negative outlook' to '2 downgrade' if political collapse materialises.

iran-us-war-directly-threatens-hormuz-fe.headline: Iran-US war directly threatens Hormuz fertilizer input flows; Houthis strike Saudi oil ports on Red Sea, blocking alternative LNG/ammonia route
iran-us-war-directly-threatens-hormuz-fe.summary: The near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz since late February 2026 and renewed Houthi strikes on Red Sea ports (including the Port of Mokha ballistic missile attack on August 15) have simultaneously blocked both of the Gulf region's primary energy and fertilizer shipping corridors. Qatar, the world's largest LNG and ammonia exporter, warned Gulf producers could halt output within days if tankers cannot transit Hormuz.

proposed_indicator.label: Hormuz/Gulf ammonia & LNG export disruption severity
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = Hormuz and Red Sea both open, fertilizer/LNG flows normal; 1 = one corridor disrupted, partial rerouting possible, price spike <20%; 2 = both Hormuz and Red Sea effectively closed to commercial tankers, Qatar/Saudi ammonia export halt threatened, price spike >20%

iran-us-war-directly-threatens-hormuz-fe.rationale: The existing s18 indicator 'Hormuz/Gulf disruption to fertilizer inputs (0 clear / 1 disrupted / 2 cut)' captures the concept, but has no current reading and critically lacks specificity about the mechanism. The Houthi closure of the Red Sea Bab al-Mandeb — Saudi Arabia's alternative export route when Hormuz is blocked — means *both* chokepoints are simultaneously compromised for the first time. Qatar's energy minister explicitly warned of production halts. This dual-chokepoint scenario is not captured by either s18 or s20 alone and warrants a dedicated compound indicator within s18 that reflects the compounding risk to ammonia/LNG specifically (not just crude). At current severity, this would score '2 = cut'.
